stories.title: Cyclone Akvan to spare most of Andhra; red alert remains for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram
stories.summary: Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, ASR and Kakinada districts of Andhra move from red to orange alert; the storm heads for landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan may not have much impact on Andhra Pradesh, since the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has revised its initial forecast and said isolated extremely heavy rainfall (red alert) is likely only in three districts, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam, on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Earlier, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Kakinada were also put on red alert.
They have now been put on orange alert for November 19.
There are no red alerts for the State on November 20, when the system is likely to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha.
But there is an orange alert for Srikakulam and Parvathipuram Manyam on November 20, since isolated very heavy rainfall is likely.

Meanwhile, the system over the west-central Bay of Bengal moved northwards at 15 kmph and was located at 8.30 a.m. over the same region, about 420 km east-southeast of Narsapur, 400 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam, 490 km south of Gopalpur and 550 km south of Puri in Odisha, and 590 km east-northeast of Chennai.

It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to the east of Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, with a maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph.
As of 12 p.m., very light to light showers had begun in Srikakulam district.
Ichchapuram recorded 12.5 mm between 8.30 a.m. and noon, the highest in the State, according to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh (DES-AP).
In the 24 hours to 8.30 a.m., no station had recorded more than 9 mm.
Thunderstorms and gales, with speeds reaching 90 to 100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph, are likely at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Thursday.
Squally winds of 30-40 kmph may prevail in Rayalaseema.

stories.headline: Karnataka will always be there for its neighbours, Shivakumar tells Naidu after cyclone help
stories.title: Karnataka will always be there for its neighbours, Shivakumar tells Naidu after cyclone help
stories.summary: Responding to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s letter of thanks for help in restoring power after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu, D.K. Shivakumar says his State will always stand by its neighbours
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has reaffirmed his State’s commitment to inter-State solidarity, saying that Karnataka was glad to extend a helping hand to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh in restoring electricity following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu.

Responding to a formal letter of appreciation from Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, he said the support went beyond mere administrative aid, adding that neighbours stand by each other, especially in times of adversity.
“For us, this was never just about extending assistance; it was about standing together for people.

We will always be there for our neighbours, just as we know they would be there for us,” the Karnataka Chief Minister said, according to a press release from the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister’s Office.

Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks came in reply to a detailed letter from Mr. Naidu, who conveyed the heartfelt gratitude of the Andhra Pradesh government and its people for Karnataka's prompt mobilisation of manpower.
Following severe infrastructure damage caused by Cyclones Arnab and Murasu, Karnataka deployed 68 batches, comprising 592 personnel, to work alongside local teams under difficult field conditions.

In his letter, Mr. Naidu outlined the scale of the restoration challenge within the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited (APCPDCL) limits alone, where power supply had to be restored in 1,333 villages and 1,852 poles had been damaged after Cyclone Arnab, and in 1,825 villages with 7,850 damaged poles following Cyclone Murasu.

Alongside Karnataka's contingent, APCPDCL had deployed 165 batches, comprising 1,580 personnel, after Arnab and 390 batches, comprising 3,292 personnel, after Murasu to execute the restoration works on a war footing.

Noting that the two neighbouring States share close geographical, economic and cultural ties, Mr. Naidu said that cooperation during extreme weather events strengthens these bonds and helps build more resilient disaster response mechanisms.

Reciprocating the goodwill, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister assured Mr. Shivakumar that his government remains equally committed to mutual support and stands ready to deploy personnel, equipment, and machinery to Karnataka in the event of any natural calamity or emergency.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Seeks Response Of ED, SFIO On Tina Ambani's Plea Seeking Disclosure Of LOC
stories.title: Delhi High Court Seeks Response Of ED, SFIO On Tina Ambani's Plea Seeking Disclosure Of LOC
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued notice on a plea filed by Tina.

A. Ambani, wife of industrialist Anil Ambani, seeking disclosure of whether any Look-Out Circular (LOC) has been issued against her by investigating agencies, including the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED).
Justice Mini Pushkarna sought response of Bureau of Immigration, ED and SFIO while listing the matter on December 08.
Ambani has also sought suspension of any such LOC, if issued against her, to enable her to travel to Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Bhutan between December 10 and December 30.

She has sought directions to the Bureau of Immigration and the investigating agencies to disclose the existence and particulars of any LOC against her, including its copy, the originating agency, the case or proceeding in which it was opened, the date of issuance, reference number, grounds recorded and present status.

Advocate Arshdeep Singh Khurana appearing for Ambani submitted that she wants to travel abroad to visit her family and friends and therefore, wants to know if any travel restrictions have been imposed against her.
He said that though the two agencies had summoned her, there are no pending summons as of now and that she has not been called any further.
“I wish to travel from December 10 to visit my family.
This is a disclosure petition that if there is an LOC, they may tell me and if there is no LOC, then it may come on record,” he said.
Appearing for ED, Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain said that two summons were issued to Ambani however she did not appear in response to either of them.

As he sought time to file a short response to the plea, Khurana told Court that Ambani had communicated to the agency her willingness to appear but was suffering from a spinal fracture at the relevant time.
He said that after her intimation, no further summons have been issued to her.

stories.headline: Here's why Rahul Gandhi rules out election boycott despite 'vote chori'
stories.title: Here's why Rahul Gandhi rules out election boycott despite 'vote chori'
stories.summary: The Congress leader said asking the Opposition to boycott elections would effectively end democracy immediately
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Indian democracy is "sacred" and the Congress is prepared to face electoral defeats until people realise that the system has been completely demolished, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said on Wednesday.

Interacting with students at the University of Chicago, Gandhi said boycotting elections over alleged flaws in the electoral system would bring an end to Indian democracy, and the Congress had no intention of taking that route.
"Indian democracy is sacred.
For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof," he said during the interaction moderated by Professor Robert Pape.
The Congress leader said asking the Opposition to boycott elections would effectively end democracy immediately.
"But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't participate in the election?' If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute.
And we don't want to end the structure of Indian democracy," Gandhi said.
He said the Congress would continue participating in the electoral process even as it sought to highlight what it considers serious shortcomings in the system.
"So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished," he said.
Gandhi's remarks come amid the Congress's continuing allegations of irregularities in the electoral process and questions over the functioning of institutions responsible for conducting elections.
The party has repeatedly raised concerns over the conduct of elections and the role of the Election Commission.
However, Gandhi made it clear that these concerns would not lead the Congress to withdraw from electoral contests.

stories.headline: What Are Interrogatories? Explained Amid INDIA Bloc's Plea To Question Election Commission On SIR
stories.title: What Are Interrogatories? Explained Amid INDIA Bloc's Plea To Question Election Commission On SIR
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: An application moved by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and other INDIA bloc leaders before the Supreme Court seeking to serve 48 interrogatories on the Election Commission of India (ECI) over its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) brought into focus an important procedural mechanism under civil law.

Governed by Order XI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), interrogatories are a set of written questions served by one litigating party upon the opposite party, with the court's permission, to obtain answers to specific factual matters relevant to the dispute.

The purpose of serving interrogatories is to obtain admissions, clarify disputed facts, and avoid unnecessary evidence in order to narrow down the scope of the litigation, to avoid wastage of precious time and expenditure in litigation.
The interrogatories sought to be served upon the ECI seek specific factual answers concerning the ECI's decision-making process.

The questions reportedly seek particulars regarding approvals by the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, dates and modes of approval, file records, whether objections or dissent were recorded, and matters concerning electoral-roll changes and related processes.

The Supreme Court has not yet granted leave to serve interrogatories on the ECI, and has adjourned the matter till December 9, after the ECI objected to the petitioners' application, stating that a final call on the petitioner's application to serve interrogatories would be taken after hearing both sides.
What are interrogatories?
Order XI Rule 1 CPC provides that a plaintiff or defendant may, with the leave of the court, deliver interrogatories in writing for examination of the opposite party.
The provision requires interrogatories to indicate which questions each person is required to answer.
It also restricts a party from delivering more than one set of interrogatories to the same party without an order of the court.
Importantly, the questions which do not relate to matters in controversy are deemed irrelevant, even if they might otherwise be admissible during oral cross-examination.

“Provided also that interrogatories which do not relate to any matters in question in the suit shall be deemed irrelevant, notwithstanding that they might be admissible on the oral cross-examination of a witness.” the second proviso of Rule 1 says.

stories.headline: PM Modi honours former PM Indira Gandhi on birth anniversary
stories.title: PM Modi honours former PM Indira Gandhi on birth anniversary
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 19 : Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, remembering her contribution to the country. Taking to the social media platform X, PM Modi wrote, "Paying tribute to former Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi Ji on her birth anniversary." Indira Gandhi, popularly known as the 'Iron Lady of India', was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, into a Kashmiri Pandit family. She was the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, and Kamala Nehru. She served as the Prime Minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from January 1980 until her assassination in 1984. She became a member of the Rajya Sabha in August 1964 and served until February 1967. Subsequently, she was elected to the Lok Sabha and remained a member during its fourth, fifth and sixth terms. Indira Gandhi was India's second-longest-serving Prime Minister after her father, Jawaharlal Nehru. She was known for several significant economic and social measures, including the nationalisation of banks and the abolition of privy purses granted to former princely states. One of the most defining moments of her tenure was her leadership during the 1971 India-Pakistan war, which resulted in the creation of Bangladesh. Her role in the conflict established her reputation as a decisive leader with strong political resolve. National Integration Day is observed annually on November 19 to mark her birth anniversary and commemorate her contributions to national unity and integration. Throughout her political career, Gandhi emphasised the importance of bringing together people from diverse regions, cultures and communities under a common national identity. Her policies and political approach focused on strengthening India's unity and advancing its development. Indira Gandhi was assassinated on October 31, 1984, by two of her bodyguards, months after she ordered Operation Bluestar. The military operation was launched to flush out armed separatists who had taken shelter inside the Golden Temple in Amritsar, one of Sikhism's holiest shrines. (IANS)

stories.headline: Jaishankar flags 'weaponisation' of resources at India-Japan 2+2 talks
stories.title: Jaishankar flags 'weaponisation' of resources at India-Japan 2+2 talks
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Thursday flagged the growing "weaponisation" of connectivity, resources and supply chains, and called for stronger India-Japan cooperation amid global uncertainty and a complex Indo-Pacific strategic landscape. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh are in Tokyo for the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue, known as the 2+2 meeting, held on Thursday. A bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe upheld the High Court's decision to quash the Chief Secretary's June 2022 order and the consequential demand notice of September 2022.
The matter pertains to land of Gaursons' predecessors-in-interest, which the Housing Board acquired for its Vasundhara Scheme in Ghaziabad.

After years of litigation, the Housing Board executed a second Exchange Deed in 2016, giving Gaursons alternative land in the Siddharth Vihar Yojana.

The growth achieved in other fields is completely negated by the negative impact from this manageable dereliction by all the stakeholders.”, the Court observed.
"There is a need to emphasise that poor sanitation and solid waste management affect the outlook of our society and country.
There are instances where similar economies, within India and outside India, have succeeded in their sanitation and hygiene objectives.
Our existing resources make it possible, albeit through unwavering implementation by the statutory enforcing authorities and adherence by the citizens," the Court added.

While pointing out deficiencies in the progress report, a bench of Justice S.V.N. Bhatti and Justice N.V. Anjaria on November 17 directed District Collectors across the country to use drone surveys and video-call inspections to monitor implementation of the SWM Rules and assess ground-level conditions at waste management facilities.

The Court also directed Chief Secretaries of States to ensure District Collectors upload geotagged, timestamped photographs showing the status of facilities in urban and rural local bodies as of November 21, 2026, and their progress as of January 1, 2027.
The Court noted that approximately 400 districts were yet to establish Special Cells to assist District Collectors.

Only nine out of 28 States had met the target for urban bylaws, while 16 States had not reported the incorporation of rural bylaws and 18 States had not reported four-way segregation of rural solid waste.

It also flagged inadequate reporting on notices issued to residential, commercial and business establishments for non-compliance, and the lack of information on public-private participation and waste-to-energy initiatives.

stories.title: Delhi SIR : Supreme Court Asks ECI To Verify Complaint Of False Form 7s Filed To Delete Mustafabad Voters
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19) directed the Election Commission of India and the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer to verify a complaint submitted by Congress leader Ali Mehdi regarding the filing of alleged fraudulent Form 7 applications seeking the deletion of voters in the Mustafabad constituency in Delhi during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.
Necessary remedial steps have to be taken if the allegations are found to be true, the Court added.

With this direction, the bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana disposed of the writ petition filed by Mehdi, without expressing anything on the merits of the allegations.
The petition was filed relying upon reports published by The Hindu as per which most Booth Level Agents (BLAs), in whose names the Form 7 applications were filed, denied signing them.

There were also reports that the voters, against whom the Form 7 applications were filed on the ground that they were either dead or shifted, were very much alive and were living at their given addresses.
Against this backdrop, the petition was filed, contending that Form 7 applications were not filed by genuine objectors, and were filed against genuine voters.
The petitioner relied on the report that 28 electors, against whom deletion applications were filed, were actually living at the given addresses.
The petitioner's counsel submitted during the hearing that out of the 37 Form 7s filed, 36 turned out to be false.
During the hearing, the bench observed that the Election Commission of India has no control over the BLAs, who are the agents of the political parties.
"If a booth-level agent makes a fraudulent application, the Election Commission can blacklist him.
Beyond that, they have no control," Justice Bagchi said.
The petitioner pointed out that in the UP SIR, the Court had asked the ECI to act against the bulk filing of fake Form 7s.

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notice to advocate Pravin Singhal on a plea filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) seeking initiation of criminal contempt proceedings against him for allegedly making insulting remarks against Chief Justice of India (CJI), Surya Kant, in open court.

A special three-judge Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta, Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said that it was prima facie satisfied that the SCBA's motion for initiation of contempt proceedings, along with the alleged attempt to scandalise the judiciary, required to be taken forward.
"Issue notice, returnable on January 20, 2027," ordered the Justice Datta-led Bench.
The apex court directed Singhal to file his reply by January 8, 2027, and any rejoinder by January 13.
It further directed advocate Singhal to remain personally present before the top court on the next date of hearing.

During the hearing, SCBA President and senior advocate Pradeep Rai submitted that the incident, which took place on November 16, involved deeply disrespectful conduct and could not be allowed to go unchecked.
"We have to deal with this with an iron hand.
This cannot be allowed," Rai submitted.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who was present in the courtroom, also supported the plea, saying that the majesty of the Supreme Court could not be compromised.
"I would fully support the petitioner.
The majesty of this court cannot be compromised," SG Mehta submitted.
The Justice Datta-led Bench said it would require the assistance of the Solicitor General, the Centre's second highest law officer, when the matter is taken up next.

stories.headline: Amit Shah inaugurates key anti-terror conference; deliberations to focus on cross-border terrorism
stories.title: Amit Shah inaugurates key anti-terror conference; deliberations to focus on cross-border terrorism
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 19: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday inaugurated a two-day key anti-terror conference, which will deliberate on "cross-border terrorism" besides the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges, among others. Held annually, the conference has steadily grown into a significant gathering of operational forces, agencies working in the field of counter-terrorism, and experts from the technical, legal and forensic domains. It offers the agencies/forces an opportunity to collectively examine matters that have bearing on national security and the threats arising from terrorism. In keeping with the 'whole of government approach', the conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders. It seeks to establish formal as well as informal channels that enable coordinated and concerted action against terrorism. The conference also aims at contributing substantive inputs towards the formulation of future policy, a statement issued by the Home Ministry has said. The conference sessions will address a range of subjects, including obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations, and the effective management of trials, it said. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation and emerging hybrid threats to national security. "Further sessions will examine the tools, techniques and case experiences involved in disrupting terror financing networks, as well as the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges," said the statement issued on Wednesday. The conference is being organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) as a part of a continued effort to bolster the nation's collective response to terrorism. This year's conference deliberates on the theme "cross-border terrorism", it said. The conference will also host a capacity-building training programme for state police personnel and practising professionals. The programme has been designed to equip participants in several areas. These include applying the new criminal laws in terror investigations, using digital evidence in prosecution, and trial strategy and management. "The programme will also cover special provisions relating to the investigation of terror cases, common challenges posed by the defence, the protection of witnesses, and the initiatives taken by the government to improve prosecution," the statement said. Over the two days, the deliberations will enable law enforcement agencies to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations. The conference is being attended by senior police officers of states and Union Territories, officers of central agencies and departments dealing with counter-terrorism, and experts from allied fields including law, forensics and technology.
